#2684. Lions scouting report: Patriots’ strengths, weaknesses

For the first time since 2015, the Detroit Lions are heading overseas! The Lions have played only two international games in their history—going 1-1 in London, England—but this time they're headed to Munich, Germany. Entering this matchup, they've won four straight games and want to keep that streak alive while claiming their first-ever win in Germany.

Detroit takes on the New England Patriots, who appear to be in a rough spot right now, losing two of their last three games and barely above .500. Coming off a Super Bowl appearance last season, New England is currently the seven seed in the AFC, and with injuries also piling up, they've got a lot to overcome to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Let's take a deep look at the Patriots' season so far as they head into Week 10.

Week 1: Lost to Seattle Seahawks 13-10Week 2: Defeated Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3Week 3: Lost to Jacksonville Jaguars 35-6Week 4: Defeated Buffalo Bills 29-26Week 5: Defeated Las Vegas Raiders 45-17Week 6: Defeated New York Jets 26-19Week 7: Lost to Chicago Bears 30-24Week 8: Defeated Miami Dolphins 24-19Week 9: Lost to Green Bay Packers 45-27

Quarterback Drake Maye has had a rocky performance after being an MVP finalist last season. He had a rough first month, throwing "meatball subs," as the kids say nowadays. Maye played well but had an abysmal Week 9, throwing three interceptions. This season, Maye is averaging 253.6 yards per game with 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, tied for the league lead in interceptions.

The Patriots' running game has been lackluster this season. Second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson is in a sophomore slump, compounded by injuries, with just 203 yards, a touchdown, and 3.9 yards per carry. Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson hasn't been explosive either, averaging 3.9 yards per carry with 399 yards and two touchdowns—and he could be held out of this game with a knee tendon issue. The team has seen a little bit of life in third-string back Corey Kiner, who is averaging 4.9 yards per carry with 244 yards and a touchdown.

At receiver, it's been an interesting ride: the Patriots traded for wide receiver A.J. Brown to be their top receiver after losing Stefon Diggs in free agency, and Brown has battled ankle injuries, playing in only three games with 101 yards on nine catches. The top receiver currently is DeMario Douglas, who leads the team in yards (434) and touchdowns (four). The Patriots also signed Romeo Doubs in free agency to a big contract, and he is currently on IR, though he will return this season—he's got 261 yards and three touchdowns in 2026.

One reason for the running game struggles is injuries on the offensive line. The Patriots are without both starting guards, Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker, and now left guard Ben Brown will most likely miss this week's game, according to head coach Mike Vrabel. PFF ranks them 19th in run blocking (62.7), which plays a big part in why the running backs can't find success on the ground. With them not having success on the ground, that puts more pressure on Maye to air it out, and suddenly he's turnover-happy, trying to make plays for the offense.

On defense, the front seven has done a solid job overall. EDGE Elijah Ponder leads the team with 7.5 sacks and is tied for fourth-most in the NFL. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore has 4.5 sacks while rookie EDGE Gabe Jacas has 3.0.

The secondary has been about average, as newly extended cornerback Christian Gonzalez has six pass deflections and a 51.4 PFF coverage grade. Former Lions cornerback Carlton Davis III has been doing well, with a 72 coverage grade. Nickelback Marcus Jones has played well, tied with Gonzalez for the team-leading six pass deflections, and earned a 59.5 coverage grade.

New England is allowing a 67.5 percent completion percentage, the third-highest in the NFL, and is just nine yards behind the Lions for most passing yards allowed this season (2,256), according to Next Gen Stats. They've allowed some big plays in the air, including 32 20+ yard passing plays (second-most) and seven 40+ passing-yard plays (tied for fourth-most). Despite the pass rush getting home, it isn't getting there fast enough for the secondary to hold up its end of the bargain. With teams struggling to run against New England, they've had to air it out and risk that pressure, and the secondary has had its share of woes.

Key players ruled out: WR Romeo Doubs (IR), G Mike Onwenu (IR), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (IR), LB Harold Landry III (PUP)Key players to monitor: WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), LT Will Campbell (knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee)

Injuries have started to pile up for the Patriots over the past few weeks. It started after Week 1 when A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury and went to IR. He has returned from IR but has played only two games, as the injury is still bothering him. He has missed the last two games and, according to Tom Pelissero, should return sooner rather than later, perhaps after the Week 11 bye.

In his absence, Doubs and Mack Hollins stepped up but also suffered injuries: Hollins just returned from IR in Week 9, while Doubs is set to return from IR after the team's bye week. The interior offensive line has seen both starting guards, Onwenu and Vera-Tucker, land on IR, with Vera-Tucker likely returning this season, though Onwenu's status remains up in the air. New England is still waiting to activate linebacker Harold Landry III off PUP as well.

Week 9 was a bad week for New England injuries, starting with Henderson having a medical emergency that forced him to miss the game; his status is unknown. On the field, the Patriots saw four starters go down, all with knee injuries. Left tackle Will Campbell, Stevenson, Davis III, and Brown all left the game and didn't return with their injuries. Campbell told the media after the game that he's fine, while Vrabel didn't provide an update on Stevenson or Davis III on Monday.

New England's defense has been helping this team a lot, especially in stopping the run and getting to the quarterback. Starting with the pass rush, New England has 25 sacks overall, tied for ninth most in the league. Ponder has been playing lights out and has given this defense a big spark in their pass-rushing abilities. PFF grades them with an 82.8 pass rush grade, second-highest in the NFL.

This front seven can do more than get to the quarterback; they can also slow down the running game. They've allowed an average of 3.9 yards per carry, tied for ninth-fewest. More impressively, though, they've allowed only one run over 20 yards, for 34. This team makes it really hard to run the football and dares you to drop back to throw it.

When you're forced to air it out, that pass rush comes into play and pressures your quarterback. It's a seesaw battle opposing offenses have to deal with. Do you go aggressive and try to run on them, or lean on your passing game to hopefully light it up? If the passing game succeeds, it opens the door for the run game to have a better chance of breaking one through; if you can't do either, it's going to be a long day for your offense.

While the data and numbers show the Patriots offense is average to slightly above average, injuries are piling up on that side of the ball. Maye has barely had his top two wide receivers together, and now possibly both of his top two running backs could be missing time as well. It doesn't help that the team is already down two starting guards, and one of their replacements won't be playing. Campbell has been playing great at left tackle, so if he somehow misses this game, it could really hurt New England's chances at winning.

Maye hasn't been consistent, and it's hard when you don't have all five starters in front of you for protection and your top weapons on the sidelines. New England has leaned on him to help with ground-game struggles, but with Hollins and Douglas as the top receivers, it's tougher to expect much production than with Brown and Doubs. Maye is doing all he can, but he's taken a step back from last season.

These injuries are piling up, and sure, some of the players will return and aren't gone for the year, but if they don't return soon, there might be nothing left to play for when they do. The AFC isn't as dominant as the NFC, so New England can afford a few losses, but you don't have an avalanche to start, and suddenly it's December and fans are waiting for the 2027 NFL Draft in April.

Key matchup: Lions ground attack vs. Patriots front seven

This matchup will likely determine who wins this football game. While Detroit's ground attack hasn't had many big plays yet, the longest being a 30-yard rush, it's still a strong part of who they are as an offense. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is having a solid season and making his case for MVP consideration. Detroit averages 4.4 yards per carry and has found the end zone 10 times on the ground.

I mentioned earlier how the Patriots' run defense has been solid, and this will be a good-on-good battle. Detroit has a plethora of weapons in the passing game, and they can win through quarterback Jared Goff if need be. Against the Packers last week, the Patriots allowed 372 passing yards, and Detroit's strong passing attack could give the Patriots secondary PTSD. While Detroit can lean on the passing game, that doesn't mean it wants to, and it will keep trying to run the ball on this Patriots front seven. If Detroit can break through this unit and move the ball on the ground, that opens the door for the passing game to find success too.

If New England holds its ground and keeps opposing running backs down, Detroit could run into trouble. In their two losses, Gibbs totaled 98 rushing yards and only one touchdown on the ground. Detroit's offense can survive a rough Gibbs game, but we haven't seen them do it so far in 2026. If the Patriots can contain Gibbs, Detroit could have a long flight home.

Vegas line for Sunday: Lions favored by 2.5

#2683. Füllkrug addresses age concerns after returning to Germany squad under Klopp

Topping the Bundesliga's scoring charts with nine goals for Werder Bremen, Niclas Füllkrug has been recalled to the Germany squad by Jürgen Klopp for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia on Friday and the Netherlands on Monday.

A few weeks before announcing his latest squad, Klopp seemed to suggest that Füllkrug's age of 33 was a disadvantage as he looks to build a Germany team for the future.

"Niclas Füllkrug scores goal after goal in the Bundesliga, but he's 33. That's not my fault," Klopp said in an interview with DAZN last month.

"We have the present, the medium-term future and the long-term future. In the present, it can of course work; in the medium term, possibly as well. Long term, well, we'll have to see."

While Klopp has since admitted that he is "not thrilled" with the statements he made in that interview, Füllkrug himself addressed his age at a press conference on Monday.

"My age is a fact, but it's not something I think about too much. I've spoken to the head coach about it and I didn't take his comments personally in the slightest," he said.

"We're at a stage where the focus is on developing young players. We've got several players who are really making an impression at the moment, so there are plenty of options to choose from."

Overall, the West Ham loanee is simply happy to be back in the squad for the first time in over a year.

"I'm delighted to be back. It's recognition of the work you put in and how you perform for your club. It's great to be part of the national team again and to have the chance to train under Jürgen Klopp," he said.

"I've caught up with a lot of familiar faces and met plenty of new ones too. The squad looks very different now and you can really feel how much has changed. I'm happy that I can just be myself and that people respond positively to that."

#2681. Klopp set to hold talks with Nmecha over controversial religious celebration

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is expected to hold talks with Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha after the midfielder's controversial crown celebration sparked debate over the weekend, according to Bild.

When Nmecha bagged a brace in Borussia Dortmund's 2-1 win over SV Elversberg on Saturday, he celebrated by kneeling down, removing an imaginary crown and placing it on the ground.

The celebration is associated with the evangelical network “Ballers in God”, which LGBTQ+ organisations have classified as “Christian fundamentalist”, and its campaign “The King's Return”.

According to research by, among others, ARD's Monitor programme, parts of the religious group hold homophobic and anti-LGBTQ+ views and describe abortion as “Satan's plan”.

The celebration prompted Borussia Dortmund's Supporters Council to criticise the midfielder over the weekend and call on the club to clearly distance itself from evangelical networks.

Now, with Nmecha joining the German national team for the upcoming international fixtures as part of Jürgen Klopp's 24-man squad, a conversation with the coach about the celebration is reportedly on the cards.

German Football Association sporting director Rudi Völler addressed the issue on the podcast Kerners 11.

“Of course, there is freedom of religion and freedom of belief. Everyone is free to express their faith in their own way. Some people like it, others don't. Naturally, we will speak to him about it again, because it has now become a public issue. The most important thing with an issue like this is that you first have to understand it properly. We have to ensure that the processes surrounding these matters are handled correctly," Völler said, via Bild.

“So far, I can only say positive things about Felix. He did an outstanding job at the World Cup – not just as a footballer, but also in the way he behaved between matches. He is extremely popular with his teammates and is a thoroughly decent person.

“But I can understand the debate and that not everyone likes it. As I said, we will handle it in a similar way to Dortmund – we are in contact with them. But we shouldn't blow it out of proportion either. We will certainly speak to him about it.”

Nmecha also performed the celebration after scoring in Germany's 7-1 win over Curaçao at last summer's World Cup.

#2679. Week 9, 3 up and 3 down: A disappointing result triggers a sell-off

The Atlanta Falcons Spanish expedition was fruitless, and the team returned to the States with another L to their name. The front office responded by doing something we haven't seen in years: sell off assets. There were role players with good contributions to highlight, but a handful of starters let the team down.

The Falcons are 3-6, and while they are technically in play for the NFC South title, that's not good enough for Cunningham, and that's a refreshing mentality. It's never easy losing a player like Jessie Bates, but with free agency looming and the team being far from a Super Bowl-caliber roster, Cunningham made the trade with an eye toward the future, collecting a 2nd and 5th-round pick.

He also made a buzzer-beater trade that shipped Ryan Neuzil to the Ravens and netted the team a 2028 6th-round pick and Andrew Vorhees. Neuzil doesn't fit this new scheme, and instead of getting nothing for him and knowing the comp formula wouldn't go their way with future spending, the GM took a proactive approach.

Woerner has been pretty steady after a slow start and had himself a respectable game. While the Falcons run game has been in a slump, it's not due to him. On the Falcons best runs you'll almost always find Woerner in the mix. He wins most of his battles against opposing linebackers and can be quite stout on the edge. It was nice to see the team reward him early with a touchdown.

He still needs to work on that Tush Push, but that's gonna be hard to do behind the centers on the roster, especially when Dexter Lawrence is across from you.

London is a bargain for what he provides. His presence was felt against the Bengals; he had two pressures, a sack, and a tough run stop on the goal line. Year after year, he's proven he can handle double teams and make plays off pure effort.

He's a glue guy that plays with an edge, and every roster needs guys like these. London is playing on a one-year deal and looks like a no-brainer for a new contract in 2027.

Terrell got worked early and often in this matchup. Ja'Marr Chase picked up where he left off in the 2019 National Championship, and had his way with Terrell. Tee Higgins was also able to haul in a touchdown on the corner. Man, press, zone—it didn't matter what the coverage was; Terrell got scorched. It has been somewhat of a down year for the corner, who spent time on IR, but this game has fans irate.

I understand where they're coming from, but this did happen against the best QB-WR pair in the league, and it's not like the Falcons are better off without Terrell, for now. Still, his days as a top-flight corner in this league are fading.

It was another rough performance for the linebacker, who has taken a massive step back during his second year in Atlanta. I respect his willingness to play through injury, but it's hurting the team, and his odds of getting anything more than a cheap one-year deal somewhere in 2027. He can't even perform a form tackle right now.

If it was just his body breaking down, that'd be one thing, but his coverage drops have been sloppy, and he isn't diagnosing plays close to the speed he was last year. He may have been an X-factor in 2025, but he is one of the weak links in 2026.

I begged for Folk to be cut and Cunningham delivered. It was one thing when the missed kicks happened from the 50s, but from 38?! Folk will still be remembered as one of the best to do it over the past decade, but unfortunately he ran out of gas when he got to Atlanta.

The Falcons are 3-6 and without some familiar names heading into Week 10. The team is in full evaluation mode, and while it's hard to get excited about that in-season, it's the right call.

#2677. NBA power rankings: Luka Dončić, Lakers on a tear as top team shifts again

It has been three weeks since the 2026-27 NBA regular season opened and there have already been three different teams to top this list.

That has been the state of play thus far, as no team has begun to separate itself as a dominant force – at least not yet.

But if there is one theme that has emerged, it's that potent offenses are ruling the day, and no player has been leading his team's scoring more than Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić, who is putting up Wilt Chamberlain-like numbers.

Here are the Week 3 USA TODAY Sports NBA power rankings:

Though he has been inefficient, rookie Darius Acuff Jr. has been a bright spot. There haven't been many others.

As they have most of the season, the Bulls remain dead last in net rating and it's not even close, with an abysmally poor mark of -16.2. In fact, they're ranked dead last in several major metrics.

Practically all of their impact veterans are injured, and coach Will Hardy even appeared to mouth to himself on the sidelines during a recent game about how bad Utah has been.

Losers of seven consecutive, the Bucks have faced tough competition recently. Either way, the offense, which ranks 29th in points per game with 106.3, isn't capable enough to compete with below-average teams, either.

They simply have not found a third (or fourth) scoring option behind Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle.

As long as the Clippers continue to commit turnovers at the pace they do – 18.5 per game – the offense won't be able to sustain consistency.

It looks like that four-game win streak in the middle of the second week of the season was a mirage; the Pels have now lost three consecutive and allowed 138.5 points per game over their last two.

Since Tyrese Haliburton went down with a left hamstring strain, the Pacers have gone 1-6.

No team has a worse shooting percentage in the NBA than Charlotte, which is converting baskets at just 40%, a full 10 points lower than the Lakers (50.7%), the squad leading the category.

It looks like this team just won't be competitive without Paolo Banchero, who has now missed seven games.

There had been some promise – AJ Dybantsa has flashed some nifty moves at times – but a four-game losing skid has zapped any juice from these new-look Wizards.

It has been a wildly inconsistent start of the season for the Suns, who are suffering from the dip in scoring by Dillon Brooks. He's averaging 14.9 points per game, down from 20.2 last season.

In a recent game, the Hornets were missing three starters, two of whom are their best scorers: Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller and Moussa Diabate. The full-strength Cavs lost by 12.

The Grizzlies have cooled off a touch since their blazing start to the season, losing three of their last four.

Things have certainly been better since that horrid start, and they have had some tough defensive luck, but defensive rebounding, consistency with their 3-point shooting and finding a secondary scorer to complement Giannis Antetokounmpo are still issues.

They've lacked pop and don't have a single victory over a team with a winning record.

After essentially alternating wins and losses, it appears the Raptors may be getting some good news, as Kawhi Leonard (knee swelling) is due to be reevaluated soon.

It's clear the Mavericks are going to have flashes of brilliance when Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving are in sync the way they've been this week.

They're continuing to share the ball, leading the NBA in assist-to-turnover ratio (2.10) and assists per game (31.7), and they've won four of their last five.

They've won four in a row. The offense has been solid, though certainly not as crisp as it was during their magical postseason run.

After topping this list last week, Houston went just 1-2 and the common thread was a starting five that lacked the scoring pop it had in the first two weeks of the season.

After dropping their first three games of the season, the Warriors have ripped off eight consecutive and Stephen Curry, at 38 years old, has played his way into the (very, very early) MVP conversation.

Without Jalen Duren (hamstring), Cade Cunningham's assist numbers are down significantly, from 9.9 per game last season, to 7.6.

They had a brutal stretch of games against the Lakers, Spurs and Thunder. They went 1-2 and now have Oklahoma City, the team Portland toppled Tuesday, in a two-day back-to-back.

With all their injuries, there are just going to be nights like Tuesday, when Shai Gilgeous-Alexander simply didn't have enough to outgun the shot-happy Trail Blazers.

Even with Anthony Edwards (knee) out for an extended period, the Timberwolves have remained competitive and Ayo Dosunmu, who's averaging 23.8 points per game over his last five, has stepped up nicely.

Perhaps Jaylen Brown allowed emotion to dictate his approach Tuesday against the Celtics. One other key issue in that loss: the Sixers uncharacteristically allowed turnovers to snowball into 21 points off of those giveaways.

In the first true test about whether Boston made the right choice to ship Jaylen Brown to the 76ers, Paul George erupted for 36 points and made six 3s while Brown struggled through early foul trouble to only 13 points.

They own the NBA's longest winning streak at nine games, Victor Wembanyama is back to posting absolutely monster stat lines and San Antonio is playing with excellent cohesion.

They may not be generating a ton of assists relative to their made field goals, but Luka Dončić (39.3 points per game) is on a historic start and overseeing the NBA's best offense, which is averaging 121.5 points per 100 possessions.

#2676. NHL Power Rankings: Flyers flounder to start new season as Rick Tocchet searches for answers

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Philadelphia opened the season with a 7-0 loss to the rival Pittsburgh Penguins, and coach Rick Tocchet described his team's play as "disturbing." There was only one way for the season to go after that, right? Wrong.

The Flyers are off to an 0-2-2 start, and the underlying numbers aren't pretty. Per Natural Stat Trick, they have a five-on-five expected goals share of 26.0%, which ranks last in the NHL. Their 4.57 xGA/60 also ranks last. Their 1.94 xGF/60? You guessed it. Last.

Tocchet's bunch entered the season with a lot of well-earned optimism. Even with subpar play from Matvei Michkov last season, the Flyers managed to reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2675. Week 10 Fantasy Football Mailbag: Should Managers Add Fernando Mendoza?

The NFL trade deadline is in the rearview mirror, and a few moves altered the fantasy football landscape. Kirk Cousins reunited with the Minnesota Vikings, Keenan Allen was traded to the San Francisco 49ers, and Josh Downs was sent to the Kansas City Chiefs.

In this week's installment of our fantasy football mailbag, which questions are eating away at managers?

Note: Feel free to reach out to me on Twitter so I can answer your fantasy football questions in future articles.

All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) practices before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

With Cousins traded to the Vikings, the Fernando Mendoza era is set to begin for the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10. Ahead of his first career start, should fantasy managers add Mendoza?

In superflex leagues, fantasy managers should scoop up Mendoza if he's available. While Mendoza is viable in deeper leagues for desperate managers, it may be worth waiting to start him.

Mendoza will be thrown into the fire to begin his career, facing the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos in his first two starts. The Seahawks and Broncos are both 10th or better in dropback EPA allowed.

Things get easier for Mendoza after the Raiders' bye in Week 13, as he'll face the Los Angeles Chargers, Tennessee Titans, and Arizona Cardinals in three of his final five games. The Titans and Cardinals are 27th or worse in dropback EPA allowed, while the Chargers are 17th.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) warms up before the game against the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Justin Jefferson, Josh Downs, and Keenan Allen were the WRs most affected during the NFL trade deadline. Where should each of them rank moving forward?

Entering Week 10, Jefferson is the WR31 in fantasy points per game (11.9). However, with Cousins throwing passes to Jefferson again, there's no reason to rank Jefferson outside the top 10 WRs anymore.

Jefferson was the WR2 in fantasy points per game (21.7) in 2022 with Cousins as his QB.

Downs is the WR61 in fantasy points per game (8.3) playing in a below-average Indianapolis Colts offense. But with Downs going from Daniel Jones to Patrick Mahomes, Downs could soon move into the WR3 or flex range.

While Downs' metrics are disappointing this year, there's a non-zero chance he becomes the No. 1 target for Mahomes over Rashee Rice before the season concludes.

The 49ers have been shorthanded at WR in recent weeks, so Allen is primed for a decent-sized role immediately. If Mike Evans and/or Deebo Samuel are inactive again in Week 10, Allen could be a WR3 or flex option as a slot target for Brock Purdy.

Once San Francisco's wideouts are healthy, Allen and Samuel will be ranked similarly, while Evans would still be the top option in the passing game.

Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride (85) spikes the ball after a touchdown catch against the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect

The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals are both dealing with a bevy of injuries on offense, limiting the viable pass-catchers available. With the Rams and Cardinals facing each other in Week 10, can managers trust any pass-catchers from either team?

On the Rams side of the equation, Tyler Higbee is in the best position to succeed with Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Terrance Ferguson sidelined. While I'd avoid starting any of the Rams WRs, rookie CJ Daniels is a name to watch if he gets more playing time.

As for the Cardinals, Trey McBride is still a must-start TE, though his ceiling could be lowered with rookie Carson Beck expected to start at QB. At the same time, Michael Wilson is out for the rest of the season, which could be viewed as a positive or negative for McBride managers.

Amid other injuries at WR, the Cardinals will trot out a wideout trio of Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, and Devin Duvernay. None of them should be trusted in any format right now.

Hopefully everyone's fantasy football squads enjoy plenty of success in Week 10!

#2671. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2670. 7 great NFL rookies are who already changing their teams’ future

The consensus entering the 2026 NFL Draft was that the class was light on top-end, elite talent — but incredibly deep when it came to finding reliable starters. Now we're at the midpoint of the season it's time to check in and see how the rooks are progressing.

Broadly speaking, we've seen an incredible depth of defensive talent come out from the 2026 class, but the offensive side is a lot trickier to pin down. The Raiders are taking a slow, measured approach to elevating Fernando Mendoza to starter at quarterback; the season has been objectively horrible for Jeremiyah Love in Arizona, and the top receivers are struggling inside mediocre offenses to really drive the point home.

Today we look at the best rookies from the season so far, and who has the inside track for the end of season awards.

The race for offensive rookie of the year has come down to three receivers, and Denzel Boston is in the driver's seat. The 39th pick has been incredible for the Browns in spite of having horrible quarterbacks feeding him the ball, and he's within earshot of the same numbers that 2025 OROY Tetairoa McMillan put up a year ago. Here are their comparative stats over the first nine games of their career:

Tetairoa McMillan (2025): 41 receptions, 558 yards (13.6 YPC), 2 TDDenzel Boston (2026): 32 receptions, 507 yards (15.8 YPC), 3 TD

It's wild that this might be the second straight year we have seen an Offensive Rookie of the Year receiver who was underrated in the draft process. Boston does a phenomenal job using his frame to high-point the ball and fight through contact, but like McMillan, his route running and separation were vastly underrated during the pre-draft process. Right now he's the offensive steal of the draft, and should win the OROY unless something dramatic happens.

The Titans are still a work in progress, and it's unclear if Cam Ward will ever become "the guy" at quarterback — but at least Tate is looking like the correct pick. Tate has 413 receiving yards, including 18 receptions for a first down through seven games and five starts. That's fairly astonishing when you consider that Ward only has 1,483 passing yards on the season — meaning that Tate has accounted for over a quarter of all air yards, despite missing two games.

While the skills are definitely there, ball security is something the rookie needs to work on. Tate has fumbled three times this season after the catch, and while they haven't been back-breaking plays, this is an area where he could improve. That won't affect his rookie of the year chances, but there is some ground to be made up in order to pass Boston, and the Titans' passing game isn't doing him any favors.

It's a testament to how bad the Browns' QB room is that they have two of the top offensive rookies, and yet Cleveland ranks 29th in scoring and 20th in passing yards.

Concepcion is a receiver made for a good quarterback to leverage. That's been the biggest knock against him so far. Right now he has 437 receiving yards and 1 TD — but it should be so much more based on how open he's getting, as well as his unreal ability to carve up zone coverage.

The numbers are very good, and Concepcion is picking up steam this season, but as less of a big-play receiver it's trickier to get noticed in comparison to his teammate. Mark my words though: When the Browns find a real QB he will elevate to become their best offensive weapon.

Arvell Reese is exactly who we thought he was, and that's a very good thing for the New York Giants. A do-everything defensive Swiss army knife, Reese has been the biggest x-factor on a Giants defense that is extremely scary, albeit still a work in progress.

The rookie has stuffed the stat sheet in almost every area. He has 49 tackles, 4.5 sacks, 32 run stops, 1 forced fumble, and 1 interception. If you need anything on defense, Reese is going to give you it. It feels like we're not just witnessing the best rookie defender of 2026, but potentially the best defensive player to enter the league since Myles Garrett — that's how good Arvell Reese has been.

Home run pick, and he's going to run away with the DROY this year.

The Jets got clowned on a little when they took David Bailey with the No. 2 overall pick and left Reese on the board, but he's been phenomenal for them. Sure, he might not have the same all-around game as the Giants' linebacker, but with 7.5 sacks so far this season he's emerged as the primary pass rusher on the team.

Bailey has been great at both generating pressures and sealing the edge against runs. He's trending as a Top 20 EDGE in the NFL this season in both areas, which is phenomenal for a rookie to achieve. In any normal season he would be the runaway favorite to win the end of season award, but as it stands he might need to eclipse 15.0 sacks to get noticed or hope that Reese falls off at the top.

Despite recent headlines when Trey McBride tried to stunt on Caleb Downs, the Cowboys' rookie safety has been really, really good this season. He ranks highly among all NFL safeties in pressures and run stops, while also being one of the most reliable solo tacklers at the position.

There are some weaknesses to his game, most notably diagnosing and interrupting pass plays — but we knew that was an area he needed to work on during the draft process. Overall Dallas got a very good player who will anchor the defense for years to come, but it's a very hard sell on end of year awards when it comes to defensive backs — largely because they don't stuff the stat sheet in a way that attracts voters.

It's been incredibly easy to ignore the Dolphins this season. In fact, it's better for your health if you ignore this team — even if you're a die-hard fan. One bright spot has been 2nd round pick Jacob Rodriguez, who is proving to be every bit the tackling machine in the NFL that he was in college.

With 79 total tackles this season, Rodriguez is on pace for 168 combined when the dust settles. He's even shown glimpses of pass-rushing chops from the middle of the field, adding a handful of pressures for good measure — which wasn't really in his skill set.

The Dolphins have been desperate to get that Zach Taylor-esque leader in the middle of the field for some time now, and they've got their guy. He won't do a lot that's eye-popping, but that's also a good thing, because like a true old-school middle linebacker it's best if they do their job and get quiet stops, rather than hearing their name while making big plays, and giving them up in equal measure.

#2669. Andy Reid’s Tenured Professor Era Sparks Chiefs Fans Debate

Andy Reid has entered a phase where he acts like a tenured professor who is tired of student questions. The Kansas City Chiefs head coach has made it clear that he does not enjoy answering the same inquiries from the media week after week. This attitude was on full display after the team defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday. While the win ended a two-game losing streak, the postgame interaction highlighted a growing divide between the coach and the people asking about his decisions.

The coach has plenty of passion for his players and still shows creativity on the field, but his public demeanor has changed. He now tells reporters exactly what he will and will not discuss. This shift has led to frustration among fans who feel he is avoiding accountability for recent struggles. The situation has become a weekly occurrence where Reid cuts off questions before they are fully formed, creating an air of dismissal toward the press corps.

One of the main topics Reid refuses to discuss is the job security of kicker Harrison Butker. The veteran kicker has struggled with long-distance field goals this season. Since 2024, Butker has made only 45 percent of his field goals from 50 yards or more. At a 69.5 percent rate, every other NFL kicker is converting these attempts. Despite these poor numbers, Reid told reporters he would not make any decisions on the spot during the press conference.

Reid opened his remarks by stating that he knew he would be asked about Butker. He said he would address the situation as the week goes on and that there is no need for reporters to ask the question again. He made it clear that he would look at everything before making a move. This response was accepted by the media, as not a single reporter pushed him on the issue during the session.

Following Butker's failure to convert two additional field goals before halftime in the matchup versus the Jets, reluctance to tackle the kicker's performance has emerged. One of those misses was rendered moot because an offside penalty was called on the defense. Reid knew the questions would be coming, yet he chose to shut down the conversation early. This approach suggests he is protecting the player or perhaps avoiding the scrutiny that comes with making a high-profile change.

Another source of irritation for Reid is the constant questioning about left tackle Josh Simmons. A back injury sustained in mid-August caused the Chiefs player to miss the final two preseason games. Reid initially insisted the injury was minor, which became a point of discussion when Simmons missed the first regular-season game. By the time the team entered their bye week in Week 5, Simmons had not played a single snap despite being on the active roster.

Progress stalled further when a bulging disc in his back worsened the situation. He was eventually placed on injury reserve, ensuring he remains sidelined through Week 11 at the minimum. The will-he-or-won't-he nature of the update kept reporters confused and fans frustrated. Reid played coy most of the time, giving indirect and vague answers that only brought about more scrutiny.

Reid clarified his stance on confronting the reality of the injury during one update. He told reporters, according to Arrowhead Addict, "I hope this isn't asked to me every week. I mean, let's just put this to rest. He'll take care of that. This isn't that big of a story." His desire to end the line of questioning shows how much he dislikes the repetitive nature of injury updates. The communication from the team always felt indirect, which only fueled more speculation about the true state of the player's health.

Reid also made a controversial decision to bench Kingsley Suamataia at left guard in Week 8 against the Denver Broncos. He decided to play Mike Caliendo instead of the rookie lineman. Suamataia was benched for the second time, after being substituted in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders. The move signaled a lack of confidence in the young player's ability to protect the quarterback in key situations.

Fans and analysts have pointed to these benching decisions as evidence that the offensive line is not gelling. The inconsistency at the guard position has led to more pressure on the quarterback and fewer running lanes for the ball carriers. Reid's choice to go with Caliendo suggests he believes the veteran can handle the job better than the rookie. However, the move has not stopped the criticism regarding the team's offensive execution.

The benching of Suamataia adds to the list of personnel decisions that have drawn scrutiny. It is part of a pattern where Reid makes changes that confuse the fanbase. The lack of a clear explanation for why the rookie was benched has left many wondering about the criteria for playing time. This uncertainty contributes to the feeling that the team is not operating with a clear plan.

The most notable moment of the press conference came after a failed quarterback sneak during the game. On a third-and-1 in the first quarter, Reid inserted backup quarterback Justin Fields to execute a sneak. The play failed to convert, and Fields fumbled the ball. The Jets recovered the fumble and capitalized with a field goal to take an early lead. This play marked the first quarterback sneak with an actual quarterback for Kansas City since 2019.

Reid blamed the media for the failure of the play. He joked that he felt pressured by reporters to call the sneak after they criticized him for not calling one in the previous game against Denver. This remark was made in a joking tone, but it highlighted his annoyance with the constant media scrutiny.

Reid explained that the play is difficult to perfect because it is hard to practice live. He stated, "Yeah, so listen, we've got to make sure—those are hard to practice live." He added that the quarterback sneak is hard to practice unless you do it in a game. He emphasized the need to get the two players on the same page and ensure the ball gets up first in the quarterback's hands. Despite the explanation, the failed play remains a coaching error in the eyes of many.

Fans have expressed strong frustration with Reid's handling of the situation. A fan commented that a scapegoat always exists to sidestep the actual issue, which they identify as Andy Reid. The fan noted that last year it was Matt Nagy, last week it was Mike Caliendo, and this week it will be Harrison Butker. This pattern of shifting blame has angered supporters who feel the coach is not taking responsibility for the team's struggles.

Reid's reaction to the botched play drew criticism from another fan who labeled it entirely unserious behavior. They wrote that Reid gave the team the most ill-prepared quarterback sneak ever and then told them to shut up about it. The fan argued that a head coach needs to take short-yardage futility much more seriously. This sentiment reflects a growing belief that the coach is not engaged in the details of the game.

One commenter stated bluntly that the average fan fails to grasp just how terrible Andy Reid is at his job. They called the situation pathetic. A different user contended that the failed sneak indicated a coaching issue rather than a reason to abandon the play entirely. They believe the team managed to turn a simple quarterback sneak into a turnover, which is a coaching failure. These comments show a deep divide between the coach and the fanbase.

Observers have likened Reid's present condition to Bill Belichick's concluding season in New England. OutKick's Bobby Burack wrote that Reid looks more confused than ever. He characterized Reid as an all-time great coach appearing utterly baffled by the current iteration of the NFL. This comparison draws parallels to Belichick's difficult 2023 season, where the Patriots finished 4-13.

Belichick's final season was a disaster, with the team ranking bottom of the NFL offensively and averaging just 13.9 points per game. Elimination from playoff contention happened with four weeks left. signifying their earliest removal since Belichick's first season. A 24-year streak featuring six Super Bowl titles concluded due to these struggles. Critics worry that Reid is heading down a similar path of decline.

The comparison is not just about wins and losses but about the decision-making process. Reid's reluctance to call quarterback sneaks and his vague injury updates mirror the confusion seen in Belichick's final year. The team has shown flashes of dominance, but the overall execution has been inconsistent. This uncertainty has led to questions about whether Reid can adapt to the modern game.

The team also left Sunday's win with significant injury concerns. A hamstring injury struck wide receiver Xavier Worthy during the game. Patrick Mahomes absorbed a hit to his right throwing elbow during a second-quarter strip-sack. Mahomes returned before halftime and finished the game, but he admitted he wasn't throwing the ball the way he wanted to early in the second half.

Worthy has struggled to become the reliable explosive option the team envisioned. Rashee Rice lost time to a hamstring injury, while Tyquan Thornton endured a significant ankle injury. Reid and Mahomes find it harder to maintain offensive momentum without a consistent downfield threat. When the running game fails to generate ground production, the receiving corps' lack of dependable output becomes a critical problem.

General manager Brett Veach admitted prior to the trade deadline that the Chiefs were investigating the receiver market.

#2668. Could Nwaneri's lack of playing time prompt Arsenal to end Dortmund loan early?

After joining Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan deal just before the summer transfer window closed, Ethan Nwaneri was initially handed decent playing time and started four consecutive Bundesliga games between Matchdays 3 and 6.

However, the 19-year-old's playing time has decreased significantly as the season progressed, and he has played just 47 minutes across five short cameos in BVB's last six games in all competitions.

The lack of playing time is hardly ideal for Dortmund or Nwaneri himself, but it is arguably an even bigger concern for Arsenal, who sent him out on loan specifically to find regular first-team football.

Nwaneri found himself in a similar situation during the second half of last season, when he was on loan at Olympique Marseille. He made just four starts in 11 appearances and was left on the bench for his final four Ligue 1 games

With the Gunners certainly keen to avoid a repeat of that scenario, they could potentially activate the recall clause reportedly included in their agreement with Dortmund, unless Nwaneri's situation improves in the coming weeks.

German outlet Ruhr Nachrichten previously reported that, should Arsenal wish to exercise the clause, they must make their intentions clear "well before the start of the transfer window". Exactly how far in advance they need to do so, however, is unclear.

#2665. Commanders finally face true “must win” game to keep their season alive - Daily Slop

Editor's note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!

Washington will face the New York Giants on Thursday night in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Given the state of the NFC East race, it's easily the Commanders' most important game of the season. Whether they come out on top will probably dictate their fate.

While a win won't ensure anything, it would at least give Washington a chance moving forward. A loss, however, would make the team's road to the playoffs [effectively impossible].

After the Giants lost star outside linebacker Brian Burns to a torn ACL in Week 3, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson…turned up the heat. Since Week 4, New York's defense has blitzed opponents on 46.5 percent of their dropbacks (second-highest rate in the NFL). That has helped the unit generate a pressure rate of 36.4 percent (13th) and a sack rate of 9 percent (sixth).

Wilson hasn't blitzed anyone more than he did the Commanders in Week 5. They blitzed on 62.2 percent of Washington's dropbacks and sacked quarterback Jayden Daniels five times.

The Giants had a season-high seven sacks in their win over the Eagles. Although they have a talented defensive line, their most effective pass rusher has been inside linebacker Arvell Reese, who had three sacks against Philadelphia.

As the Commanders attempt to curb New York's aggression, they will have to do so with a backup at center. Starting center Lucas Patrick suffered a concussion against the Rams and won't be able to clear concussion protocol by Thursday. Veteran Nick Allegretti will start in his place against the Giants.

The Commanders are optimistic Burks (foot) will play Thursday after he sat out last week. They also believe cornerback Amik Robertson, who suffered an ankle injury late against the Rams, will be good to go.

With their season hanging in the balance in the form of a Thursday night game at the division-leading New York Giants, the Washington Commanders stood pat at the trade deadline Tuesday — a tacit acknowledgment that they're trying to salvage the tenure of coach Dan Quinn but aren't willing to part with draft picks to add to an injury-riddled group that has produced just two wins in the first half of the season.

The Commanders — at 2-5-1 — are within a victory at New York of pulling within two games of the 5-2-1 Giants. Given their tie against New York last month — a game the Commanders should have won if not for an egregious late-game management situation — it's not unreasonable that Washington [are] holding out hope to get back into a divisional race that has no surefire winner.

Now, the Commanders head into the final nine games of the season — a stretch that will determine whether Quinn gets a fourth year or not — with a roster that is thinned by injury and hasn't efficiently closed out games. The Thursday night game against the Giants provides the first test as to whether that was the right path forward.

Patrick was signed on September 16 and performed better than Allegretti, who was still nursing a calf strain early in the season, so Patrick earned the starting role. Unfortunately, Patrick left Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams with an apparent concussion. He has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the New York Giants, and Allegretti will replace him.

Rookie center Matt Gulbin replaced Patrick against the Rams on Sunday and struggled to fill the role effectively. So, it makes sense that veteran Allegretti is getting the nod. However, the issue here is why didn't the Commanders turn to Allegretti on Sunday? Quinn said after the game it was because Allegretti had been practicing at guard.

Stefon Diggs and Jer'Zhan Newton missed October's 27-27 tie; now five players from that game are on IR, leaving Washington to find answers across its offense and defensive front

The last time the Washington Commanders and New York Giants played, the game ended in a 27-27 tie after both teams missed chances to win in overtime. That day, Stefon Diggs was inactive, and Jer'Zhan (Johnny) Newton was on injured reserve. Terry McLaurin, Dyami Brown, Daron Payne, Jacory "Bill" Croskey-Merritt, and Javon Kinlaw played; all five are now on IR.

A month later, Washington has managed only one win since, and will enter the game at 2-5-1 after losing 20-13 to the Rams in Week 9.

Van Jefferson has a much bigger part in this offense now, too. He played just three offensive snaps against the Giants, compared with 36 against Los Angeles, where he caught five passes for 58 yards and a touchdown. Antonio Williams' workload has grown from 42 snaps in the tie to 52 against the Rams. Jefferson should stay involved even if Treylon Burks returns from the foot injury that kept him out Sunday. He gave Blough another weapon to work with.

The backfield has changed as well. Croskey-Merritt ran for 82 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in the first meeting. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler handled the running-back snaps against the Rams.

Daronte Jones has two substantial workloads to replace up front. Payne played 63 of Washington's 89 defensive snaps in the tie, while Kinlaw played 56. Payne also recorded a sack and a forced fumble. With both players now on IR, Washington will ask a different group to handle the interior work and create some disruption of their own.

Newton's return to the lineup helps, but his first game back also shows how much work falls on the rest of the rotation. He played 20 defensive snaps against the Rams, while Shy Tuttle played 43, Tim Settle 33, and Ricky Barber 15.

Mathematically the Commanders remain alive, but with nine games remaining, any realistic hope the team has for a strong finish likely begins and ends vs. the Giants on Thursday (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video). A win and they would be two games back with eight to play and own the tiebreaker — if that eventually mattered.

"We all know how badly we need this," Washington coach Dan Quinn said. "Everyone in this building understands that."

Another loss would drop them to 7-18-1 since the start of last season and likely intensify the speculation by analysts over Quinn's future. Owner Josh Harris has not publicly commented on Quinn's job. Quinn said he regularly meets with Harris before and after games and also on Mondays.

But in training camp, one team source said what has been repeated by others at various points: "It's a results business."

And the results need to improve. Washington has now played five one-score games; the Commanders are 1-3-1 in those games — and 3-7-1 since the start of 2025. In 2024, when they went 12-5, Washington was 8-4 in one-score games — but that included a four-game winning streak at season's end.

The Commanders were in another one Sunday before losing 20-13 to the Rams. They had the ball last, drove to the Rams' 32-yard line with eight seconds left, but two failed plays ended the threat.

They lost 23-17 in Week 6 at San Francisco, failing in the red zone — a touchdown was nullified by a face mask penalty — and again on the last series when they reached the 28 with 22 seconds to play.

"We get in those moments and we have to finish," Daniels said.

Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

The Washington Commanders defense played relatively well in the loss to the LA Rams on Sunday. They held the Rams to below their season averages for total yards, passing yards, rushing yards and points, which tells you that ultimately it was a pretty solid performance. But the Rams are dealing with a lot of injuries on offense and only really had one receiving threat in this game, star receiver Puka Nacua. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, while no other receiver had more than two catches.

So it's fair to ask if the Rams only really had one receiving threat in this game, how did the Commanders allow Nacua to be so productive? Surely you just double up on Nacua and stop the ball going his way and make others beat you? Well, it's not quite that simple unfortunately. For starters, the Rams did a great job moving him around and forcing the ball to him. Four of his 14 catches were on receiver screens, for example.

There's not really any way to stop a team throwing receiver screens if that's the way they want to force the ball to their star receiver. You'll notice that on three of those four plays, the Commanders were in a blitz look with multiple extra defenders walked up on the line of scrimmage. Those quick screens to Nacua were clearly a game plan option for the Rams to try and help deal with the Commanders tendency to load the box and send aggressive blitzes.

Ultimately, the Commanders did a pretty good job on these. Nacua gained some yards, but the first screen came on third and eight, Nacua only got six so the Commanders forced a fourth down. The second screen saw K'Lavon Chaisson punch the ball out and Nick Cross recover the fumble. The third screen came on third and 10 and Chaisson chased down Nacua to keep the gain to seven yards, again forcing another fourth down. It was only really the final one that did damage and that was just eight yards on first and 10, so that's not the end of the world either.

But that's only four of Nacua's 10 catches, so what happened on the rest. Well, there was a good mix of plays where the Commanders actually had pretty solid coverage and Matthew Stafford made a great throw or Nacua made a great catch. There were also a few plays where I think the Commanders would like to have done a better job. So let's first look at the plays where the Rams deserve credit, because I think the Commanders were pretty good on a lot of these plays.

We already exercised one demon this week with a win in Philly. That was therapeutic for me personally. I don't think we have beaten JD yet? [Note: no, the Giants have never logged a win vs Jayden Daniels] He always killssss us. [Defensive coordinator] Dennard [Wilson] looks up to the task and will hopefully have a plan for [Jayden Daniels'] running ability.

Commanders are better than their record says. No doubt high stress level close game.

I say it every week! When we rush too fast up field it leaves gaping lane for him to run. If we don't get sacks fine. We cannot let him out of the pocket. You guys think we keep rolling [on Thursday night]?

The Vikings reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders on Tuesday, sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas.

With the trade, 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' starting quarterback, beginning this week at home against the Seattle Seahawks. Aidan O'Connell will be Mendoza's backup.

Cousins posted a goodbye to the Raiders on his Instagram story, writing, "Thank you Raiders Nation! Go get em @fernandomendoza."

Trade talks between the teams didn't materialize until Tuesday, according to Las Vegas general manager John Spytek, who said the team was not actively looking to trade Cousins. Spytek said he received a few phone calls about Cousins until the most important one came from Vikings GM Nolan Teasley. He and Teasley spoke on the phone for a while to hammer down the framework on a deal that made sense for both sides.

Spytek said he did not speak to Cousins before Tuesday about the possibility of him being traded.

Willis was placed on injured reserve Tuesday due to a groin injury. With Willis shelved, second-year quarterback Kyle McCord will fill in, beginning Sunday on the road against the Indianapolis Colts.

The 27-year-old Willis, regarded as one of the best running quarterbacks in the NFL, was noticeably hobbled in his team's Week 9 defeat to the Detroit Lions.

A free-agent signing after renewing his career and promise under the tutelage of Matt LaFleur with the Green Bay Packers, Willis has shepherded a rebuilding Fins squad to mixed results. The Dolphins are 1-7 and he's completed 58.2% of his passes for 174.5 yards per game, six touchdowns, six interceptions, and rushed for 232 yards and three scores.

Drew Rosenhaus told Pat McAfee the $13 million that Aiyuk "allegedly" owes is "separate and distinct" from his playing status

Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has not yet repaid the 49ers any of the $13 million in bonus forfeiture that he "allegedly" owes the team, his agent said Tuesday.Agent Drew Rosenhaus said during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on ESPN that he will attempt to reach an agreement on Aiyuk's behalf on that matter "separate and distinct" from resolving Aiyuk's playing status.Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, and NFL commissioner Roger Goodell granted the 49ers a two-game roster exemption for him that expires Nov. 23, according to Monday's NFL daily personnel notice."Brandon will either play for the 49ers when the two weeks is up or they can decide to release him, by which he will be a free agent and I expect that there will be interest in him," Rosenhaus told McAfee. "I definitely expect him to play this season. Judging [by] the comments from coach [Kyle] Shanahan, it doesn't sound like they plan on bringing Brandon back."So when the two weeks is over, it's my job to potentially find a new team for him. And I'm confident, now that he's healthy, that he will play. As far as the money that's allegedly owed … the $13 million, whatever it is—he hasn't paid anything yet. That's something that we'll work out separate and distinct from the issue of him playing. Hopefully we'll work something out to the benefit of Brandon's and something that's fair. And that's also part of my job."Aiyuk passed his physical with the 49ers, according to Rosenhaus."I think that in all likelihood Brandon would probably sign with a team that knows him, [with] somebody that has somehow been affiliated with him, either in college or the 49ers," Rosenhaus said Tuesday. "That's just my guess 'cause, you know, there's a lot of that in the NFL. You see people connect the dots where they [have] history, where there's relationships."

[GM John] Lynch told the station that "we can talk a little more in detail about the process" this week because it is "kind of a fluid situation." He was asked whether the 49ers would listen to anything that Aiyuk and Rosenhaus might have to say about a possible reunion.

"I think everything's possible," Lynch said. "You know, I will say this: We've worked with Drew a lot. You know, Drew is a good guy to deal with. He's reasonable. He's got integrity. … That's all good. We'll see how this thing goes. I think I'll just leave it at that."

#2663. Tarik Skubal landing spots: Predicting new home for two-time Cy Young winner, the offseason's best free agent

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Arguably the best pitcher in baseball is up for grabs this winter. Tarik Skubal is a free agent for the 2026-27 MLB offseason, easily the top available on the market, and every team should be trying to earn his services. But will they? Almost certainly not.

The 29-year-old southpaw spent the first six years of his major-league career with the Detroit Tigers before being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the 2026 deadline. He won back-to-back Cy Young awards in 2024 and 2025 and earned MVP votes in both seasons. He's likely to become the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history both in total value and AAV.

Of course, the giant flashing sign floating above all of this is the expiring CBA, which will run out at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, after which the owners are expected to lock out the players until a new deal is reached. Over the summer, the league proposed limiting free agency contracts, an offer that the players' union quickly disavowed, and the owners' demand for a salary cap is the underlying throughline of every negotiation. Perhaps that means Skubal will rush to sign on the dotted line before new rules are in place. Perhaps that means teams will wait out the negotiations until they know how much they have to spend -- and how they'll be punished if they do so.

Regardless, CBS Sports' MLB experts, three people who are very much not involved in contract negotiations, have gathered to predict where Skubal lands by the time Opening Day rolls around.

Mike Axisa: I'll go off the board a bit and say the Padres. The new ownership group didn't pay $3.9 billion for the franchise only to cheap out in their first offseason. They're moneyed and motivated, and that's usually enough to land the top free agents. It should appeal to Skubal too. The Padres are in the postseason most years, they play in a great (and largely pitcher-friendly) ballpark, and it's San Diego. How can you not love San Diego? Skubal to the Padres because the new owners want to make a big splash in their first offseason. That's my prediction.

Dayn Perry: I'll say the Mets top all offers by a margin sufficient to overcome their lack of appeal compared to the usual suspects (meaning, mostly, the Dodgers). They definitely need a stabilizing force in the rotation outside of Nolan McLean, and they also need a vibes shift after the deeply disappointing 2026 campaign. Landing the biggest fish of all on the market would provide all that and meet a clear need. The Mets will already be rebound candidates in 2027, and signing the likes of Skubal would position them as contenders. Obviously, the structure of the next CBA has bearing here, but maybe this all comes together before the lockout shuts it all down for an indeterminate period of time.

Matt Snyder: I'll go with the easy and obvious answer and say the Dodgers. I don't think the owners win the fight for a salary cap, but there'll be enough push from the Dodgers' end before the CBA talks shut down free agency to snatch up all the talent they can to get his contract grandfathered before a new agreement.

As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026.

Date/Time: Thursday, November 12th, 2026 | 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey)

The 2-5-1 Washington Commanders have a short week before taking on the NFC East-leading New York Giants (5-2-1), on Thursday Night Football. While Sunday's loss to the Rams dissolved any positive feelings surrounding Washington's win over Philadelphia, the good news is the Giants barely scraped by that same team on Sunday with an ugly score of 19-11. A win on Thursday night would hand the Commanders the tie-breaker against the G-Men and narrow their division lead to only two games with 8 games left in the season.

Things have changed significantly since the two teams met in Week 5, and J.J. McCarthy is now the Giants starting quarterback. The 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, J.J. is 2-0 as a starter and proven to be clutch when called upon for Big Blue. McCarthy is 5th in the NFL in third-down completion percentage at 71.4% since Week 7. On the opposite side of the matchup, Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders have a bottom of the league third down conversion rate of 31%.

Running back Cam Skattebo was briefly on the outside looking in, but returned to John Harbaugh's good graces with a 124 yards on 17 carries performance in Week 7 against the Houston Texans. He leads the Giants with 418 rushing yards on 98 carries(4.3 ypa), and is projected to be available for Thursday's game after missing the last two weeks with a hamstring injury. Malik Nabers has continued his standout performance since his breakout game versus the Cardinals earlier in the season. Nabers had 36 receptions for 509 receiving yards and two touchdowns last month and was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. After struggling briefly, tight end Isaiah Likely has developed a strong on-field connection with McCarthy, and the duo connected for 5 receptions for 53 yards and a touchdown versus the Eagles. The Giants currently rank 14th in total offense.

The Commanders are reshuffling things yet again after center Lucas Patrick suffered a concussion on Sunday, and the team is returning to Nick Allegretti at the pivot Thursday night. While that in and of itself should be concerning for Commanders fans, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson just deployed a variety of pressure looks aimed at the center and guard positions against the Philadelphia Eagles last week.

Arvell Reese has been on a tear recently, and the first-round rookie is the only NFL player with 65+ tackles, 8+ TFL, and 1+INT on the season thus far to go along with 4.5 sacks. The Giants lost linebacker Tremaine Edmunds in Week 6, but replacement Micah McFadden has stepped up and also played well with 9 tackles, 1 sack, 2 TFLs, and a fumble recovery versus the Eagles.

Once considered a liability, the Giants' secondary has been one of the team's strengths in 2026. New York ranks among the league's best in total takeaways (9) and interceptions (6), five of which came from Giants defensive backs. Safety Jevon Holland has been playing at a high level and leads the team with three interceptions on the season. The Giants are ranked 5th in total defense.

The interior of the Giants' offensive line is questionable and could be where the Commanders' defense can attack New York's offense, even without starting DTs Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw. The Giants allowed 4 sacks and 11 pressures to the Eagles defensive line in Sunday's matchup and are tied for 27th in sacks allowed with 27 total on the season. Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out with injury during their first meeting this season. Their return to Washington's secondary for the team's second meeting should go a long way in preventing repeat performances from Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely. The development of defensive coordinator Daronte Jones should help prevent another late game collapse. The addition of Steve Wilks to the defensive coaching staff is another positive development towards that goal.

The true question marks for Thursday night surround David Blough and the team's offensive line in a game that quarterback Jayden Daniels has declared is a must-win in order to keep the Washington Commanders season alive.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2656. Will the Rams regret not making any moves at the trade deadline?

The Los Angeles Rams went all-in this offseason. Now, they're doing it again – only this time with their own guys.

Rather than bringing in some outside help at wide receiver, kicker or punt returner, the Rams are trusting the roster they built over the course of months by standing pat at the trade deadline. They didn't make a single move, passing on the opportunity to add someone like Josh Downs or Keenan Allen, both of whom were moved by the Colts.

The question is, will they regret this gamble?

It's hard to say because the Rams found themselves in a weird limbo state. On the one hand, they're more than talented enough to win the Super Bowl. On the other, they're so banged up and the loss of Puka Nacua for even four games might be too much to overcome on their path to the playoffs.

The Rams offense has been underwhelming all year with Nacua. It's scary to think about what it will look like without him catching 14 passes and seeing nearly half of Matthew Stafford's targets like he did on Sunday against the Commanders.

I mean, the Rams had 343 yards in that game, and Nacua had 170 of them. After his 150 receiving yards, the next-closest player had 20. T-W-E-N-T-Y.

No one is denying that the Rams could've used a wide receiver. Even a veteran past his prime like Allen would've been a big lift. And Downs could've helped on punt returns, too. But there would've been a cost to acquiring one of those players.

Downs cost the Chiefs a fourth- and fifth-rounder, with a seventh-rounder going back to Kansas City. Allen cost the 49ers a sixth-rounder.

Those weren't astronomical prices to pay, but for a team like the Rams that currently has just four picks in the 2027 draft and is missing its second-rounder in 2028, they were limited with the assets they could afford to trade away. Had the Rams traded their fourth- and fifth-round picks for Downs like the Chiefs did, they would've been left with one pick in the first four rounds of next year's draft (pending compensatory picks).

And for a team that will need to rebuild its roster with young talent, it can be hard to part with valuable draft picks – especially considering how often the Rams hit on mid-to-late-rounders.

There's a chance they'll regret not making a move for a receiver. Or a kicker. Or a reliable, impactful return specialist. But at the same time, it's easy to understand why they didn't. Their road to the playoffs just became a lot tougher, and it was incredibly difficult to begin with because of the quality of their opponents. Now it's just a matter of surviving the next four games (or so) until reinforcements come.

Maybe they think Davante Adams will be back right after the bye, which would be huge. Maybe Terrance Ferguson can return in Week 12, too. If that's the case, the Rams will only have to go one more game with Adams, Nacua and Ferguson all out.

Maybe that's the reason the Rams stood pat and feel confident enough in Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels – as hard as that is to believe, given their lack of involvement this season – to go a few more games as the top receivers.

The defense is more than good enough. Now it's on Sean McVay and the offense to adapt and adjust without some of their top playmakers.

This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Will the Rams regret not making any moves at the trade deadline?
